children: Oracle Corp. (ORCL, Financials), the software giant making a major push into AI infrastructure, has disclosed a new insider sale at an interesting time for the company.
CEO Michael Sicilia sold 10,882 shares on Sept. 16 for about $1.52 million, receiving $139.94 per share.
There is an important detail behind the sale. Sicilia made it under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted in December 2025, so the transaction was arranged months in advance.
A day earlier, Sicilia also gave up 25,468 shares worth about $3.69 million to cover taxes after restricted stock units vested.
He still owns roughly 149,084 Oracle shares directly, along with another 2,655 shares held by his spouse.
What makes the filing interesting is what has happened around it.

Oracle shares have fallen roughly 49% over the past year, even as the company's cloud infrastructure business has grown rapidly. That business is becoming increasingly tied to the huge amounts of computing power needed for AI.
Sicilia's planned sale does not necessarily say much about his view of Oracle's prospects.
For shareholders, the more important story is whether Oracle's accelerating cloud growth can justify the enormous amount of money the company is spending to build the infrastructure behind it.

title: Oracle's CEO just sold $1.5 million in stock as shares rebound
